function.arguments:
{"command": "cat <<'EOF' > create_figure.py
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

# Data
x = [1, 10, 100, 1000]
y = [2, 20, 200, 2000]

# Calculate error bars (10% of each y value)
yerr = [0.1 * yi for yi in y]

# Create figure
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 5), dpi=120)

# Plot the data
ax.plot(x, y, 'b--o', label='Data', color='navy', markerfacecolor='white', markeredgecolor='navy')

# Add error bars with red caps
ax.errorbar(x, y, yerr=yerr, fmt='none', ecolor='red', capsize=5, capthick=1)

# Shade vertical region from x=10 to x=100
ax.axvspan(10, 100, color='lightgray', alpha=0.3)

# Set logarithmic scales
ax.set_xscale('log')
ax.set_yscale('log')

# Set limits
ax.set_xlim(0.8, 1200)
ax.set_ylim(1, 3000)

# Turn on major and minor grids
ax.grid(True, which='both', linestyle='--', linewidth=0.5, alpha=0.7)
ax.minorticks_on()

# Annotate point (100, 200) with arrow
ax.annotate('threshold', 
            xy=(100, 200), 
            xytext=(50, 100),
            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color='black', lw=1.5),
            fontsize=10,
            bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.3', fc='white', ec='black', alpha=0.8))

# Set labels and title
ax.set_xlabel('Input Size')
ax.set_ylabel('Runtime (ms)')
ax.set_title('Scaling with Uncertainty')

# Legend in upper left
ax.legend(loc='upper left')

# Save figure
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('figure.png', dpi=120, bbox_inches='tight')
print("Figure saved as figure.png")
EOF
"}
